newsitem.title: UK: Hambros could face legal action on Co-op.
newsitem.headline: Hambros could face legal action on Co-op.

text.p: British investment Bank Hambros and law firm Travers Smith Braithwaite, who advised Andrew Regan's bid vehicle Galileo in its failed bid for the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS), could face legal action from Galileo's liquidator, newspapers said on Monday.
The liquidator, Jason Elles of accountancy firm Ernst & Young, is said to be considering suing the bank and the law firm over the quality of the advice they gave Galileo.

Last week, both Hambros and Travers Smith were forced to give public apologies to CWS over their conduct in the affair. They also made a financial settlement in return for CWS dropping legal action concerning the use of confidential CWS information leaked to Galileo by a former CWS employee.

A spokesman for Ernst & Young said the liquidator was looking at al the options and had appointed law firm Wilde Sapte to advise him. The spokesman said it was too early to speculate on what action might be taken.
